rationale: Death or ICU admission is uncommon (c6) and exposure must be read from files, so a matched case-control design with incidence density sampling is efficient (c5). Following the investigator's preference, the study starts at the tertiary ED, where files are complete and the program has run longest; enrolment date is the main exposure (c3), and prior visits and comorbidity are handled by matching and adjustment (c2). The single-site estimate elsewhere (c1) shows the precision risk. Reporting follows STROBE.
alternatives: Add the two community EDs from the start (deferred: the investigator prefers to begin where files are complete)
Before-after comparison of visit counts (refused: regression to the mean)
Following every frequent attender with file reading for all (refused: about 3,000 files)
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial of case management is not possible for a program already running; a single-site case-control study is the simplest credible start.

decision.statement: Run a matched case-control study at the tertiary ED: cases are frequent attenders who died or were admitted to ICU within 12 months of an index date from March 2023 to December 2025, with four controls per case sampled from those still at risk on the case's event date and matched on age, sex and calendar month, and enrolment before the index date read from the files.
decision.question: How should the case management program's association with death or ICU admission be estimated?

criteria.text: Hard outcomes are rare and exposure needs file reading, so a matched case-control design with incidence density sampling is efficient.
The tertiary ED alone yields too few cases for a useful estimate.

gates.requirement: Research ethics approval for the case-control protocol
gates.evidence: Approval REB-EM-2026-112 dated 2026-08-28, supplied by the investigator
Agreement DSA-2026-044 dated 2026-08-30, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Add the two community EDs from the start
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c2, c3 and c5; both gates are met on investigator-supplied records. Whether one site gives enough cases is left to the Analysis stage.

summary: Single-site matched case-control study recommended at the tertiary ED; the precision question is left open.
